title: Git and GitHub: version control and repository security
objectives: Explain how a commit history provides an audit trail for infrastructure changes.
Identify a secrets exposure risk in a repository and describe how to remediate it.

learningObjectives.statement: Explain how a commit history provides an audit trail for infrastructure changes.
Identify a secrets exposure risk in a repository and describe how to remediate it.

body.value: Git records every change to a codebase with an author, timestamp, and message. For infrastructure and security work, this history is an audit trail: you can see who changed a policy, when, and why. That traceability is a security control, not just a development convenience.

A secret committed to a repository is compromised, even if you delete it in the next commit. The history remains. Rotate the credential immediately, then use a secrets scanner in CI to prevent recurrence.

In AWS pipelines, Git events trigger CodePipeline runs. The IAM role that the pipeline assumes should follow least privilege: it needs only the permissions required for that specific deployment, not broad administrative access.
